next_step: Finalize 48h soak + SLA draft, procurement approval by 2026-03-20
notes:
Summary: Enterprise POC focused on Dedicated capacity sizing, throughput guarantees and SLA negotiation. Customer is replacing an in-house inference cluster used for chat-based customer support + product reranking. Primary asks: deterministic tail latency, clear reserved GPU planning, and commercial SLA with credits.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-05: Lead created from trade show, initial qualification (Jordan).
- 2025-11-18: Discovery call — high-level requirements captured (Priya joined).
- 2026-01-12: Architecture workshop — discussed VPC/private control plane, KMS, logging retention. Action: run network checklist.
- 2026-01-28: Sent POC runbook + test corpus (customer support queries, product titles, long descriptions). Drive link shared.
- 2026-02-08: Security questionnaire submitted by Voyager SecOps (SOC2 evidence request).
- 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting for Dedicated POC (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_98765). Defined test matrix.
- 2026-02-22: Baseline runs on hosted API to establish quality baseline (short chat, 8-32 token responses).
- 2026-02-24: Dedicated cluster provisioned (alpha infra): 4 nodes, 8x A40 48GB equiv per node for POC.
- 2026-02-26: Load tests (k6 + custom client) run: peak steady-state simulated 120 concurrent chat sessions, 400 qps for embeddings batch=32.
- 2026-02-27: Observed 95th latency = 180ms for short chat path (tokens 8-32) at 120 concurrent; 99th spikiness to 360ms during batch spikes. Logged results in Drive sheet.
- 2026-02-28: Soak test (6h) found KV cache warm-up improved p95 by ~25% after 40 minutes. Request to run 48h soak next.
- 2026-03-02: Follow-up design session: customer requests guaranteed p95 <= 150ms for chat and burst capacity to handle 2x peak for Black Friday-style events. (Fireflies ff_2026-03-02_102341)
- 2026-03-05: Commercial ask: SLA with 99.95% uptime, 95th latency SLOs with credits, and predictable reserved GPU pricing.

POC test matrix / representative prompts:
- Short chat (support quick answers): ~12 token responses, full RTT measured; traffic model = 120 concurrent sessions, target p95 < 150ms.
- Long-form summarization: 1k-2k token inputs, blended throughput test to validate KV-cache/attention memory.
- Embeddings pipeline: batched 64 inputs, 512-d model (customer uses mixed embeddings), expected throughput = 350 qps batch-normalized.
- Reranking: cross-encoder style on top-20 candidates, latency budget per query = 250ms.

Key POC observations (raw):
- Throughput: Dedicated 4-node test sustained ~1.8k effective requests/min for chat workload with batch-friendly routing.
- Latency: p50 ~40ms, p95 ~180ms during initial runs; after cache tuning and kernel selection suggestions from Redwood Optimize, p95 dropped to ~130ms in follow-up runs at same concurrency.
- Soak behavior: 6h soak showed steady-state after ~40m; recommended 48h soak before final sizing to capture diurnal variance and GC events.
- Cost/Reserved planning: preliminary sizing suggests production reserve of 12-16 A100-80GB equiv GPUs for current traffic plus 2x burst capacity for seasonal peaks; pricing ask sent to sales.
- Failure modes: noisy-neighbor spikes on colocated batch jobs caused 99th spikes — mitigation via strict tenant isolation scheduling and priority queues.

Security / compliance notes:
- Voyager requires SSO/SAML + KMS integration and 7-year audit logging retention for some product lines. Data residency: US-only for PII workloads. Legal wants explicit data deletion workflow documented.

SLA negotiation items under discussion:
- Uptime target: customer requests 99.95% with credits; legal counters on definitions of downtime for rolling upgrades.
- Latency SLOs: p95 targets per workload class (short chat, reranking, embeddings) with separate measurement windows.
- Remedies: service credits tiered by incident duration, plus engineering time SLAs for P1s.

Open action items / next steps:
- Run 48h soak on Dedicated cluster with production corpus (owner: Priya) — target start 2026-03-07.
- Produce final sizing recommendation and reserved GPU quote (owner: Jordan) — deliver by 2026-03-12.
- Draft SLA appendix covering latency SLOs and credit formula (owner: Legal + Sales) — ready for review 2026-03-15.
- Procurement: Voyager to submit purchase order and complete CISO sign-off (blocker).

Notes style: shorthand, meeting paraphrases, links to artifacts included above. "We need deterministic tail latencies for support chat; can't have occasional 300-400ms spikes" — paraphrase from CTO call.

Relevant artifacts: load test scripts in Drive, k6 scenario + custom loader, POC runbook, measurement dashboard snapshots (link in drive).

Recommended Redwood guidance shared with customer: enable prefix/KV caching, pin model shims, enable dedicated priority queues for low-latency routes, try bfloat16 quantization for reranking models, and schedule maintenance windows for upgrades.

Sales context: likely conversion to Dedicated reserved contract once 48h soak passes and legal/SecOps sign-off. ARR estimate dependent on final reserved GPU count; mid-range estimate $250k-$750k.

CRM remarks (short): "POC trending positive. Main risk: procurement + SLA wording. Engineering impressed with latency improvements after cache + kernel tuning. Need procurement PO by mid-Jun to hit fiscal target."
